main_body: Thatched hut: a large stepped thatch roof slope (rows 0-36) over a plank-wall front with a central door and a shuttered window (rows 38-63)
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope, rows 0-35, lightest tone along the tier highlights, ending in a bright eave lip at rows 34-36
evidence: The roof is a big, clearly foreshortened top slope built from tiered thatch courses, like the Beodeul house roofs. A bright eave lip at rows 34-36 marks the front edge. Directly under it, rows 37-39 are dark, so the eave shades the wall. The vertical wall face below has an inset door frame, a recessed window with a shutter, and horizontal rails. Both a top surface and a front face are clearly drawn, and no receding side face appears.

style.evidence: The thatch has about five tones, with per-course highlights and straw streaks, and the wall planks carry grain and shading. The door has dark iron straps and a small latch highlight. The outer silhouette uses near-black on the roof sides, but the wall and door edges lean brown, so the outline reads as mixed. The piece has no large flat fills and is comparable to the reference at this scale. It is slightly less rich than the tiled houses.
